sections.h2: Power-to-liquid SAF needs far more hydrogen per litre than HEFA or ATJ

chart.title: Hydrogen per litre of SAF: 528 g for PtL, 40 g for HEFA and ATJ
chart.sub: Grams of H₂ consumed per litre of finished SAF, at about 0.8 kg/L density.

sections.means: Hydrogen is a required input to every SAF route, and the route chosen sets how much of it each litre needs.
sections.todo: Compare SAF routes on grams of hydrogen per litre as well as on price, because the draw differs so widely between them.

sections.h2: At the 2030 mandate, a PtL-heavy supply would need far more green hydrogen

chart.title: Meeting the 2030 5% blend: 40 kt of hydrogen via HEFA/ATJ, 528 kt via PtL
chart.sub: Green hydrogen needed for about 800 kt of SAF (100 crore litres), by supply route.

sections.means: The same 2030 blending target needs more than thirteen times as much green hydrogen under a PtL-heavy mix.
sections.todo: Plan near-term hydrogen supply around HEFA and ATJ, and build PtL capacity only once it is committed at scale.

sections.h2: PtL SAF costs several times more per litre than HEFA or PBtL SAF

chart.title: PtL at $8–10 a litre sits well above HEFA at about $1.45 and PBtL at $1.41
chart.sub: Indicative SAF cost per litre, by pathway and hydrogen price.
chart.source: Xynteo (2026); Berkeley-based India Energy & Climate Center; trade press.

sections.means: Hydrogen-heavy SAF becomes affordable at the mandate's volumes only once green hydrogen nears its $1.50–2.50/kg target range.
sections.todo: Tie SAF blending targets to the green hydrogen price curve rather than treating the two as separate policy questions.
